title: Tim Cook passes the baton in Apple's Q3 2026 earnings call
gist: Apple posted $109.42 billion in Q3 2026 revenue with iPhone units up 22 percent, yet the stock fell about eight percent after hours because services revenue slipped and Cook warned memory costs will keep rising into the next quarter and beyond. It was Cook's last earnings call before John Ternus takes over.

themes.theme: Segment results: hardware beat, services miss

insights.claim: Apple reported $109.42 billion in total Q3 2026 revenue, with iPhone at $54.25 billion on a 22 percent increase in iPhone sales, Mac at $10.35 billion, iPad at $6.19 billion, wearables at $7.88 billion, and services at $30.74 billion.
insights.speaker: Samuel Axon
insights.so_what: iPhone remains roughly half of revenue and is accelerating, but services—the high-margin growth narrative—is the segment that determines multiple.
insights.locator: As for specific numbers, iPhone revenue was

insights.claim: Services revenue slipped downward and disappointed expectations, which was a primary driver of the negative reception despite better-than-anticipated iPhone results.
insights.speaker: Samuel Axon
insights.so_what: A services decline breaks the 'hardware installed base compounds into recurring revenue' thesis that supports Apple's premium multiple—watch whether it recurs next quarter.
insights.locator: but its revenue for services—like Apple TV

insights.claim: Apple credited a strong Mac quarter in many regions partly to the MacBook Neo, a stripped-down, more affordable entry-level SKU.
insights.speaker: Samuel Axon
insights.so_what: Downmarket SKU extension is working as a volume lever—but mix shift toward cheaper units pressures ASPs just as component costs climb.
insights.locator: Apple also noted that the Mac had a very strong quarter

themes.theme: Memory cost shock as the forward risk

insights.claim: Apple has already raised prices on many products in response to a global mismatch between supply and demand for memory, and chip manufacturing capacity is also tight.
insights.speaker: Samuel Axon
insights.so_what: Confirms the memory shortage is passing through to end-consumer pricing at the largest hardware buyer in the world—inflationary for the whole device complex, favorable for memory suppliers.
insights.locator: Apple has already raised many of its products’ prices

insights.claim: Cook said Apple expects memory costs to continue increasing into the next quarter and beyond, and that the situation could continue to impact the business.
insights.speaker: Samuel Axon
insights.so_what: Management guiding to sustained input-cost inflation is the single most tradeable line in the call—implies margin pressure or further price hikes into fiscal 2027.
insights.locator: Cook said while taking questions on the call

insights.claim: This quarter contained only some of the memory-cost impact and likely does not reflect the full brunt of it, meaning reported results understate the coming pressure.
insights.speaker: Samuel Axon
insights.so_what: Beat-quality is lower than headline suggests; a lagged cost pass-through argues against extrapolating current margins.
insights.quote: This quarter contained some of that impact, but it likely does not reflect the full brunt of it.
insights.locator: Significant price increases could lead to lower overall sales

insights.claim: Potential Mac buyers may defer purchases for several months hoping prices come back down, creating a demand-destruction risk on top of the cost problem.
insights.speaker: Samuel Axon
insights.so_what: Deferral risk means price hikes may not fully protect revenue—watch Mac unit trends as the early-warning segment.
insights.locator: Many potential Mac buyers might choose to wait

insights.claim: Apple has not yet raised iPhone prices, leaving that lever unused and the largest revenue line still exposed to the cost squeeze.
insights.speaker: Samuel Axon
insights.so_what: An unpulled pricing lever on 50 percent of revenue is the key binary for next-year estimates—either margin compression or a demand test.
insights.locator: Apple hasn’t yet raised iPhone prices

insights.claim: Apple's stock slid around eight percent in after-hours trading despite relatively strong iPhone and Mac sales, with investors weighing soft services against supply constraints and memory costs.
insights.speaker: Samuel Axon
insights.so_what: An eight percent drawdown on a revenue beat shows the market is now pricing input costs and services trajectory, not device volumes.
insights.locator: relatively strong iPhone and Mac sales in this quarter didn’t stop

insights.claim: This was Tim Cook's final earnings call, with John Ternus leading the next quarter's call, and Cook described the transition as going seamlessly.
insights.speaker: Samuel Axon
insights.so_what: A CEO handoff landing exactly as cost inflation bites means the new management gets judged on a hard quarter—raises the odds of a kitchen-sink reset.
insights.quote: As you know, this will be my final earnings call, and John will lead these calls going forward.
insights.locator: I just wanted to take a moment to say thank you
